the mechanical excitation method is a promising method for measuring the extensive elastic compliance, loss factor and mechanical quality factor of piezoelectric ceramics.

the mechanical excitation method can measure the additional intensive parameters, including the elastic compliance and mechanical quality factor of the composite piezoelectric sample, which cannot be obtained by the conventional electrical excitation method.
The proposed method can be used to obtain the extensive physical parameters of piezoelectric ceramics.

the development of the piezoelectric materials characterization method for the partial-electrode sample, which can be applied to measure the extensive parameters directly, and to obtain more accurate values for the intensive parameters.
the direct loss measurement of piezoelectric material using the mechanical excitation method.
the development of a new piezoelectric material characterization technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mechanical excitation method can be used to obtain all the intensive and extensive parameters of the piezoelectric material, which cannot be directly measured by the electrical excitation method, such as the mechanical quality factor, the mechanical loss factor and the mechanical compliance.
the mechanical excitation method with partial electrode configuration can be a powerful and useful tool for measuring the extensive elastic compliance, loss factor and quality factor.

the mechanical excitation method with partial electrode samples can provide more physical parameters than the conventional electrical excitation method and can be a good alternative for measuring the direct loss factor of piezoelectric materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical excitation method is more accurate and more efficient for determining the physical parameters of piezoelectric materials than electrical excitation method.

it is possible to measure the loss of piezoelectric material using mechanical excitation.
